block.txt: Energy and Other Legislation Amendment (Renewable Energy Infrastructure) Bill 2026 (No 2) [Non-government Bill— Mr J H Griffin, MP]
An Act to co-ordinate investment in new generation, storage and network infrastructure in New South Wales; and for other purposes.
This Act is the Electricity Infrastructure Investment Act 2020.
This Act commences on a day or days to be appointed by proclamation.
The objects of this Act are—
to improve the affordability, reliability, security and sustainability of electricity supply, and
to co-ordinate investment in new generation, storage, network and related infrastructure, and
to encourage investment in new generation, storage, network and related infrastructure by reducing risk for investors, and
to foster local community support for investment in new generation, storage, network and related infrastructure, and
to support economic development and manufacturing, and
to create employment, including employment for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and
to invest in education and training, and
to promote local industry, manufacturing and jobs, and
to promote export opportunities for generation, storage and network technology.
The following objects also apply to Parts 4–6—

to promote consultation and negotiation with the traditional Aboriginal owners of land on which generation, storage and network infrastructure is proposed to be constructed or operated under this Act.
A person or body exercising a function under this Act must do so in a way that is consistent with the objects of this Act.

heading.b: Consultation and negotiation with local Aboriginal communities

block.txt: The Minister is to issue guidelines about consultation and negotiation with the local Aboriginal community in relation to relevant projects for the purposes of increasing employment and income opportunities for the local Aboriginal community.
The Minister is to take the guidelines into account when exercising the Minister’s functions under Part 5, Division 2.
To give effect to the guidelines, the Minister may impose a condition on a direction under section 32 or an authorisation under section 36(2).
The consumer trustee is to take the guidelines into account when exercising the consumer trustee’s functions under Part 6, Divisions 3 and 4.
The infrastructure planner must take the guidelines into account when exercising the following functions—
a function under Part 5,
a function prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this section as a function in relation to which the infrastructure planner must, when exercising, take the guidelines into account.
To give effect to the guidelines, the infrastructure planner must—
make the appointment of a network operator under section 31A(1) subject to conditions the infrastructure planner considers necessary to give effect to the guidelines, and

include, in a recommendation to the Minister under section 31B(1), details of conditions to which the infrastructure planner considers the direction should be made subject to give effect to the guidelines.
The guidelines are to be published on the Department’s website.
In this section—
local Aboriginal community includes—
an Aboriginal person who has native title rights and interests, within the meaning of the Native Title Act 1993 of the Commonwealth, in relation to the land to which the relevant project relates, and
the Local Aboriginal Land Council for the area to which the relevant project relates, and
other Aboriginal persons prescribed by the regulations.
relevant project means—
a REZ network infrastructure project or priority network infrastructure project, and
an infrastructure project to which an LTES agreement applies.
The Dictionary defines words used in this Act.
The Interpretation Act 1987 contains definitions and other provisions that affect the interpretation and application of this Act.
In this Part—
board means the board for manufacturing and construction in the NSW renewable energy sector established under section 7.
plan means a plan prepared by the board and approved by the Minister under section 8.

As soon as practicable after the commencement of this section, the Minister is to establish a board for the NSW renewable energy sector, in particular in relation to the operation of the sector and the manufacture and construction of infrastructure in the sector.
The board is to consist of—
persons appointed by the Minister, including at least 1 person representing each of the following groups—
manufacturers of steel, aluminium and other similar materials,
the metal fabrication industry,
the Australian Workers’ Union,
the Electrical Trades Union,
the Australian Manufacturing Workers’ Union,
the Mining and Energy Union,
employers in the electricity, manufacturing and construction sectors,
persons involved in the planning, design, construction and operation of generation infrastructure,
NSW electricity customers, and
the Energy Corporation, and
other persons appointed by the Minister.
The Minister is to appoint as joint chairperson of the board—
one person appointed under subsection (2)(a)(iii)–(vi), and
one person appointed under subsection (2)(a)(ix).
The board has the following functions—

to prepare and provide to the Minister a plan for the NSW renewable energy sector, in particular in relation to the operation of the sector and the manufacture and construction of infrastructure in the sector.
to monitor and review the plan and make recommendations to the Minister about the implementation of the plan,
to report to the Minister on another matter if requested by Parliament by resolution of both Houses of Parliament.
The board is to meet at least once every 6 months.
The board is to provide to the Minister a report on the board’s activities—
by 31 March 2021, and
by 30 June 2021, and
by 30 June of each following financial year.
The regulations may make further provision for or with respect to the membership, procedures and functions of the board, including the terms and condition of appointment of members.

heading.b: Plan for NSW renewable energy sector

block.txt: The plan required to be prepared by the board under section 7(4)(a) is to set out how to achieve the following objectives in relation to the construction of generation, storage and network infrastructure carried out under this Act in a cost effective way—
to maximise the use of locally produced and supplied goods and services,
to maximise the employment of suitable qualified local workers,
to foster opportunities for apprentices and trainees,
other objectives prescribed by the regulations.
The board is to provide the plan to the Minister and to make any amendments requested by the Minister.
The Minister may approve the plan only on the recommendation of the regulator.
The regulator may recommend a board’s plan to the Minister only if satisfied that the plan—
protects the financial interests of NSW electricity customers, and
is consistent with Australia’s international trade obligations, and,
promotes social and economic benefits for the NSW community and economy.
A plan approved by the Minister must be published on the Department’s website and takes effect on the day it is published.
The board may propose an amendment to the plan by giving written notice of the proposed amendment to the Minister.
The Minister may ask the board to make changes to the proposed amendment the Minister considers appropriate.
The board must make any changes to the proposed amendment requested by the Minister.
The Minister may only approve an amendment to the plan on the recommendation of the regulator.
The regulator may only recommend an amendment to the Minister if the regulator is satisfied the proposed amendment—
protects the financial interests of NSW electricity customers, and
is consistent with Australia’s international trade obligations, and
promotes social and economic benefits for the NSW community and economy.
The Minister must take the plan into account when exercising the Minister’s functions under this Act.
The consumer trustee must take the plan into account when exercising the consumer trustee’s functions under Part 6, Divisions 3 and 4.
The infrastructure planner must take the plan into account when exercising the following functions—
a function under Part 5,
a function prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this section as a function in relation to which the consumer trustee must, when exercising, take the plan into account.
To give effect to the plan, the infrastructure planner must—
make the appointment of a network operator under section 31A(1) subject to conditions the infrastructure planner considers necessary to give effect to the plan, and
include, in a recommendation to the Minister under section 31B(1), details of conditions to which the infrastructure planner considers the direction should be made subject to give effect to the plan.
As soon as practicable after the commencement of this section, the Minister is to appoint a person or body as the electricity infrastructure jobs advocate.
The electricity infrastructure jobs advocate is to advise the Minister about—

strategies and incentives to encourage investment, development, workforce development, employment, education and training in the energy sector in the Hunter and Central Coast, Illawarra, Far West and Central West regions of New South Wales, and
road, rail and port infrastructure required in the regions specified in paragraph (a) to promote export opportunities for generation, storage and network technology, and
other matters requested by the Minister.
The electricity infrastructure jobs advocate is to provide the Minister with a report on the advocate’s activities—
as soon as practicable after being appointed, and
once a year after the first report.

heading.b: Appointment of electricity infrastructure jobs advocate

block.txt: The electricity infrastructure jobs advocate holds office for the term, not exceeding 5 years, specified in the instrument of appointment, but is eligible for re-appointment.
The office may be a full-time or part-time office, as specified in the instrument of appointment.
The employment of the electricity infrastructure jobs advocate is, subject to this Act, to be governed by a contract of employment between the advocate and the Minister.
In the exercise of functions under this Act, the electricity infrastructure jobs advocate is not subject to the direction or control of the Minister.
The regulations may make further provision for or with respect to the appointment of the electricity infrastructure jobs advocate, including the terms and conditions of appointment.

heading.b: Setting and monitoring of energy security targets
Energy security target monitor to set and monitor targets

block.txt: The energy security target monitor is to calculate an energy security target for each of the following 10 financial years using the following formula—
maximum demand is the forecast peak demand for megawatts of electricity used by NSW electricity customers, based on a 10% probability of exceedance (POE) forecast methodology.
A 10% POE forecast is expected to be exceeded, on average, 1 year in 10 years.

reserve margin is the sum of the amount of megawatts of electricity capable of being produced by the 2 generating units in the State that are capable of producing the largest amounts of megawatts of electricity according to AEMO for the financial year or a different amount prescribed by the regulations.
The energy security target monitor is to assess and monitor whether or not the firm capacity will meet the energy security target for a financial year.
The regulations may prescribe—
the factors to be considered in calculating the maximum demand, and
the method for calculating the maximum demand.
In this section—
generating unit has the same meaning as in the National Electricity Rules.
The energy security target monitor is to report to the Minister about the energy security targets.
A report is to be provided to the Minister—
once a year, no later than 60 days after AEMO publishes a statement of opportunities under the National Electricity Rules, and
at any time the Minister requests a report.
A report must include the following—
the energy security target for each of the following 10 financial years and how they were calculated,
the firm capacity for each of the following 10 financial years and how they were calculated,
an assessment of whether or not the firm capacity will meet the energy security target over the following 10 financial years,
for a financial year in which the energy security target monitor considers the firm capacity will not meet the energy security target (a target breach)—
the expected size of the target breach in megawatts, and
the expected duration of the target breach,
information that may assist the Minister in considering what action, if any, the Minister intends to take in relation to a target breach,
other information the energy security target monitor considers relevant,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
In preparing the report, the energy security target monitor must—
consult with the Secretary and AEMO, and
take into account any matters prescribed by the regulations.
The energy security target monitor must, if requested by the Minister, provide additional information or a clarification of a report.
Before providing the information or clarification, the energy security target monitor must consult with the Secretary and AEMO.

The energy security target monitor may provide a further report to the Minister that contains additional information or revises information contained in a previous report if the monitor considers it necessary because of a change in relevant circumstances.
Subsections (3) and (4) do not apply to a further report under subsection (7).

heading.b: Publication of energy security target monitor reports

block.txt: An energy security target monitor report is to be published on the Department’s website no later than 60 days after it is given to the Minister.

Before the report is published, the energy security target monitor must amend the report so that it does not contain information the disclosure of which could, in the opinion of the monitor, reasonably be expected to—
diminish the competitive commercial value of the information to the person who provided the information to the monitor, or
prejudice the legitimate business, commercial, professional or financial interests of the person who provided the information to the monitor.

heading.b: Minister to consider energy security target monitor reports

block.txt: As soon as practicable after receiving an energy security target monitor report from the monitor, the Minister must consider what action, if any, the Minister intends to take in response to the report.
The Minister may prepare a statement about what action the Minister intends to take and must make the statement publicly available.

heading.b: Energy security target monitor’s information gathering powers
Requirements to provide information to energy security target monitor

block.txt: The energy security target monitor may, by written notice to a person, require the person to provide relevant information to the monitor.
A notice under subsection (1) must specify the following—
the information required to be provided,
the form in which the information is to be provided,
the time within which the information is to be provided.

The energy security target monitor may require a person to answer questions in relation to a relevant matter if the monitor believes on reasonable grounds that the person has knowledge of the relevant matter.

The energy security target monitor may, by written notice, require a person to attend at a specified place and time to answer questions if attendance at the place is reasonably required for the questions to be properly put and answered.
The place and time at which a person may be required to attend is to be—
a place or time nominated by the person, or

if the place and time nominated is not reasonable in the circumstances or a place and time is not nominated by the person—a place and time nominated by the energy security target monitor that is reasonable in the circumstances.
Without limiting the persons who may be required to provide information or to answer questions under this section, the persons may include the following—
a person who owns, controls or operates generation infrastructure,
a person who owns, controls or operates network infrastructure,
a small generation aggregator or a market small generation aggregator,
a person who provides wholesale demand response services,
an operator of a virtual power plant,
an aggregator of distributed energy resources,
a person who supplies fuel to generation infrastructure,
a person involved in planning and designing generation infrastructure,
other registered participants.
In this section—
market small generation aggregator, registered participant and small generation aggregator have the same meanings as in the National Electricity Rules.
relevant information means information that the energy security target monitor reasonably requires to assist the monitor in exercising its functions, and may include information about the following—
current and planned construction, operation and maintenance of generation infrastructure,
current and planned network infrastructure that may affect the operation of generation infrastructure,
aggregated distributed energy resources,
wholesale demand response activities.
relevant matter means a matter in relation to which information is reasonably required to assist the energy security target monitor in exercising its functions.
A person must not, without lawful excuse, fail to comply with a requirement made of the person under section 16.
A person must not give information in purported compliance with a requirement under section 16 knowing that the information is false or misleading in a material respect.
Maximum penalty—2,000 penalty units for a corporation or 100 penalty units for an individual.
The energy security target monitor must not disclose protected information, except—
to the Minister under section 13, or
to AEMO under subsection (1A), or
as required by another law.
The energy security target monitor may disclose protected information to AEMO if the monitor considers it necessary when exercising the monitor’s functions under section 12 or 13.
AEMO must not disclose protected information disclosed to it under subsection (1A).
The Minister must not disclose protected information, except—
with the consent of the person who provided the protected information, or
to AEMO with the consent of the energy security target monitor, or
for the purposes of, or in connection with, legal proceedings arising out of this Act, or
to a person belonging to a class prescribed by the regulations, or
if the disclosure is, in the opinion of the Minister, appropriate.

The Minister is not to recommend the making of a regulation for the purposes of subsection (2)(d) unless the disclosure of the protected information to the class of persons prescribed by the regulation is, in the opinion of the Minister, appropriate.
A person to whom protected information is disclosed by the Minister must not disclose protected information, except—
with the authorisation of the Minister, and
in accordance with a direction, if any, given by the Minister to the person that imposes a condition on or restricts the disclosure.
Maximum penalty—2,000 penalty units for a corporation or 100 penalty units for an individual.
The Minister may authorise the disclosure of protected information under subsection (4) only if the disclosure is, in the opinion of the Minister, appropriate.
In this section—
appropriate, in relation to the disclosure of protected information, means—
reasonably necessary—
to assist the Minister and the Department in considering what action, if any, the Minister intends to take in relation to a target breach identified in an energy security target monitor report, or
to ensure the reliability and security of electricity supply, or
to enable the energy security target to be met, and
in the public interest.
protected information means information provided to the energy security target monitor the disclosure of which could, in the opinion of the monitor, reasonably be expected to—
diminish the competitive commercial value of the information to the person who provided the information to the monitor, or
prejudice the legitimate business, commercial, professional or financial interests of the person who provided the information to the monitor.

heading.b: Renewable energy zones, access areas and access schemes
Renewable energy zones and access areas

content.txt: pt 4, div 1, hdg: Am 2025 No 80, Sch 1[4].

heading.b: Minister may declare renewable energy zones

block.txt: The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, declare a renewable energy zone comprising—
a specified geographical area of the State, and
specified generation, storage or network infrastructure, including planned or existing infrastructure.
The network infrastructure that forms part of a renewable energy zone may extend outside the geographical area specified in the declaration.
A declaration must also include the following—
a map showing the geographical area,
the intended network capacity for network infrastructure in the renewable energy zone,
the infrastructure planner appointed by the Minister for the renewable energy zone or part of the renewable energy zone,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
The Minister may make a declaration only if the Minister—
is satisfied that it is consistent with the objects of this Act, and
has considered the following—
existing network infrastructure in the renewable energy zone and the rest of the State,
land use planning, environmental and heritage matters,
the views of the local community in the renewable energy zone,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
A declaration is to be published on the Department’s website.
The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, declare an access area comprising—
a specified geographical area of the State, and
specified generation, storage or network infrastructure, including planned or existing infrastructure.
The geographical area that forms part of the access area must not include any part of the geographical area that forms part of—
a renewable energy zone, or
another access area.
The network infrastructure that forms part of an access area may extend outside the geographical area specified in the declaration.
A declaration must include the following—
a map showing the geographical area,
the infrastructure planner appointed by the Minister for the access area or part of the access area,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
The Minister may declare an access area only if the Minister is satisfied—
making the declaration is—
consistent with the objects of this Act, and
in the public interest, and
of any other matters prescribed by the regulations.
A declaration must be published on the Department’s website.
The regulations may make further provision about the exercise of the Minister’s functions under this section.

heading.b: Procedure for declaring renewable energy zones and access areas

block.txt: Before making a declaration of a renewable energy zone or an access area, the Minister must—
consider a report from the Secretary about the potential effects of the declaration on electricity costs for NSW electricity customers, and
consider the infrastructure investment objectives and the most recent report prepared by the consumer trustee under section 45, and
consult with the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces, and
consult with AEMO, and
make a draft declaration publicly available on the Department’s website for at least 28 days.

heading.b: Applications for declarations of renewable energy zones and access areas

block.txt: The Minister may make a declaration of a renewable energy zone or an access area—
on the Minister’s own initiative, or
on the application of the consumer trustee or another person.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to an application to the Minister for a declaration of a renewable energy zone or an access area, including the following—
the form of the application,
who may make an application,
the requirements for making a valid application,
the fee payable for an application by a person other than the consumer trustee,
the information to be included in the application,
requirements for public consultation before an application is made,
the procedures for the determination of an application by the Minister.

heading.b: Amendment of renewable energy zone declaration

block.txt: The Minister may amend a declaration of a renewable energy zone only—
to expand the geographical area that forms the renewable energy zone,
to specify additional generation, storage and network infrastructure for the renewable energy zone,
to increase the intended network capacity for the renewable energy zone,
to provide further details and specifications about information contained in the declaration,
to correct a minor error or misdescription.
The Minister cannot repeal a declaration of a renewable energy zone under section 19.
The Minister may amend a declaration of an access zone for the following purposes only—
to expand the geographical area that forms the access area,
to specify additional generation, storage and network infrastructure as forming part of the access area,
to provide further details and specifications about information contained in the declaration,
to correct a minor error or misdescription.
The Minister cannot repeal a declaration of an access area under section 19A.

heading.b: Renewable energy zones in Central-West Orana, Illawarra, New England, South West and Hunter-Central Coast areas

block.txt: The Minister is to declare the following as renewable energy zones—
Central-West Orana,
Illawarra,
New England,
South West.
Hunter-Central Coast.
The indicative geographical areas of the renewable energy zones are shown on a map published on the Department’s website on the commencement of this section.
The Central-West Orana renewable energy zone has an intended network capacity of 3 gigawatts.
The New England renewable energy zone has an intended network capacity of 8 gigawatts.
The Minister is to appoint the Energy Corporation as the infrastructure planner for the Central-West Orana, Illawarra, New England, South West and Hunter-Central Coast renewable energy zones.

heading.b: Access schemes for renewable energy zones and access areas

content.txt: pt 4, div 2, hdg: Am 2025 No 80, Sch 1[12].

heading.b: Minister may declare access scheme for renewable energy zone or access area

block.txt: The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, declare the access scheme that applies—
in a renewable energy zone or part of a renewable energy zone, or
in an access area or part of an access area.
An access scheme is a scheme that—

for an access scheme under subsection (1)(a)—authorises or prohibits access to, and use of, specified network infrastructure by network operators and operators of generation and storage infrastructure in the renewable energy zone, or the part of the renewable energy zone, to which the scheme applies, or

for an access scheme under subsection (1)(b)—authorises or prohibits access to, and use of, specified network infrastructure by network operators and operators of generation and storage infrastructure in the access area, or the part of the access area, to which the scheme applies.
An access scheme must be consistent with the objects of this Act.
There may be more than one access scheme for a renewable energy zone or an access area.
A declaration may also specify the following matters in relation to the access scheme—
the person or body who is to administer the access scheme,
how access rights are to be conferred on participants, which may include contractual arrangements between participants and the infrastructure planner, the scheme financial vehicle or another person,
the terms and conditions of access rights,
the functions of the regulator in relation to the access scheme,
the rights and liabilities of the scheme financial vehicle in relation to the access scheme,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
Before making a declaration, the Minister must—
consult with the infrastructure planner and relevant operators who may be affected by the declaration, and
make a draft declaration publicly available on the Department’s website for at least 28 days, and
seek and consider submissions from the public on the draft declaration.
A declaration is to be published on the Department’s website.
The Minister is to publish guidelines on the Department’s website about the exercise of the Minister’s functions in relation to the declaration of access schemes.
Before publishing guidelines, the Minister must—
make draft guidelines publicly available on the Department’s website for at least 28 days, and
seek and consider submissions from the public on the draft guidelines.
The consumer trustee is to determine the fees payable to the scheme financial vehicle by participants in an access scheme, taking into account the following principles—
maximising financial value for NSW electricity customers,
recovering the cost of the operation of the access scheme,
optimal use of the existing and planned network infrastructure in the renewable energy zone or access area,
other principles prescribed by the regulations.
The fees determined by the consumer trustee must include a component that is to be used for a community purpose prescribed by the regulations.
The component must not be less than the minimum amount or proportion prescribed by the regulations and must not exceed the maximum amount or proportion prescribed by the regulations.
The fees determined by the consumer trustee must include a component that is to be used for an employment purpose prescribed by the regulations.
The component must not be less than the minimum amount or proportion prescribed by the regulations and must not exceed the maximum amount or proportion prescribed by the regulations.
In exercising its function under subsection (4), the consumer trustee is to seek advice from the committee established under section 34W(1)(b) of the Energy and Utilities Administration Act 1987.
In this section—
community purpose means a purpose that benefits the community in a council area that, at any time after the declaration of the access scheme, is or has been wholly or partly within—
the geographical area that forms the renewable energy zone to which the access scheme applies, or
the geographical area that forms the access area in relation to which the access scheme applies.
council area means—
an area within the meaning of the Local Government Act 1993, or
a Local Aboriginal Land Council area within the meaning of the Aboriginal Land Rights Act 1983.

employment purpose means a purpose that promotes employment, skills and training for persons who live or work in a council area that, at any time after the declaration of the access scheme, is or has been wholly or partly within—
the geographical area that forms the renewable energy zone to which the access scheme applies, or
the geographical area that forms the access area to which the access scheme applies.

heading.b: Application of National Electricity (NSW) Law and National Electricity Rules

block.txt: The regulations may modify the application of, or disapply, a provision of the National Electricity (NSW) Law or the National Electricity Rules to the extent reasonably necessary to—
enable the operation of an access scheme in a renewable energy zone or access area, and
achieve the objects of this Act.

A regulation under this section that affects the operation or safety of network infrastructure may not be made unless the Minister has consulted with distribution network service providers and transmission network service providers.
A regulation under this section that affects AEMO in the exercise of its functions may not be made without the concurrence of AEMO.

heading.b: Amendment and repeal of access scheme declaration

block.txt: The Minister may amend a declaration of an access scheme only—
to correct a minor error or misdescription, or
to provide further details and specifications about information contained in the declaration, or
if there are no participants in the access scheme immediately before the declaration is amended, or
if the amendment is made in accordance with the terms of the access scheme.
The Minister may repeal a declaration of an access scheme only if—
there are no participants in the access scheme immediately before the repeal, or
the repeal is made in accordance with the terms of the access scheme.

heading.b: Orders prohibiting connection to network infrastructure

block.txt: The infrastructure planner may, by order served on a relevant operator, prohibit the relevant operator from allowing a proponent to connect proposed infrastructure to the relevant operator’s network infrastructure.
An order is to apply to network infrastructure in a specified area within a renewable energy zone.
Before making an order, the infrastructure planner must seek and consider submissions from—
the relevant operator and other relevant operators in the local area, and
the proponent, and
the local council in the local area.
The infrastructure planner must not make an order unless satisfied that—
there is significant opposition from the community in the local area to the proposed infrastructure, and
making the order is reasonably necessary to maintain community support in the local area for other infrastructure in the renewable energy zone, and
making the order is in the public interest.
An order may not be made if the proponent has development consent under the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 to construct and operate the proposed infrastructure.
The infrastructure planner is to publish guidelines on its website about the exercise of its functions under this section.
The Energy Corporation is appointed as the infrastructure planner to exercise the functions under this section for a renewable energy zone or part of a renewable energy zone.
In this section—
local area means the area in which the proposed infrastructure will be located.
proponent means a person or body who proposes to construct or operate proposed infrastructure.
proposed infrastructure means proposed generation or storage infrastructure with a capacity of at least 30 megawatts.
In this part—
authorised REZ network infrastructure project means a REZ network infrastructure project the consumer trustee has authorised under section 30AA(1)(a).
carry out an infrastructure project includes carrying out one or more of the following activities or organising, arranging for or causing the activity to be carried out—
the planning, design, financing, commissioning, development or construction of the project and other preparatory activities in connection with the infrastructure project,
an activity in connection with the ownership or control of infrastructure under the infrastructure project,
the operation or maintenance of infrastructure under the infrastructure project,
other activities in connection with the infrastructure project as prescribed by the regulations.
infrastructure investment objectives report means a report about the infrastructure investment objectives prepared and published by the consumer trustee under section 45.
infrastructure project means—
a REZ network infrastructure project, or
a priority network infrastructure project.

maximum capital costs amount, for an authorised REZ network infrastructure project, means the maximum capital costs amount for the project set by the consumer trustee under section 31(1) and as amended from time to time under section 31(2).
In this part, a reference to an infrastructure project includes a part or stage of an infrastructure project.

heading.b: Assessment and authorisation of REZ network infrastructure projects

content.txt: pt 5, div 1, hdg: Am 2025 No 80, Sch 1[20].

heading.b: Infrastructure planner to recommend REZ network infrastructure projects for renewable energy zone

block.txt: The infrastructure planner for a renewable energy zone must—
assess REZ network infrastructure projects required for the renewable energy zone, and
based on those assessments, recommend REZ network infrastructure projects to the consumer trustee for authorisation.

The infrastructure planner must publish a summary of each recommendation made by the infrastructure planner under subsection (1)(b) on a publicly available website maintained by the infrastructure planner.
The infrastructure planner must assess the following—
the different options for REZ network infrastructure projects to provide the intended network capacity for the renewable energy zone,
staging and sequencing of REZ network infrastructure projects,
funding, procurement and cost recovery for the recommended REZ network infrastructure projects,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
A recommendation by the infrastructure planner under subsection (1)(b)—
may relate to one or more REZ network infrastructure projects that the infrastructure planner recommends be authorised, and
must include recommendations about the following—
the staging and sequencing of the REZ network infrastructure project or projects,
the funding and cost recovery for the REZ network infrastructure project or projects,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
If the infrastructure planner considers it appropriate, the infrastructure planner may do either or both of the following—
recommend the consumer trustee amend the terms of the authorisation of a REZ network infrastructure project,
ask the consumer trustee to amend the maximum capital costs amount for an authorised REZ network infrastructure project.
In assessing and making recommendations about REZ network infrastructure projects, the infrastructure planner must consult with the following—
AEMO,
relevant operators in the renewable energy zone,
each local council in the renewable energy zone.
The infrastructure planner must make recommendations about REZ network infrastructure projects to the consumer trustee within the period specified by the consumer trustee.
The regulations may make further provision for or with respect to the following—
the exercise of the infrastructure planner’s functions under this section,
requiring the consumer trustee to provide information to the infrastructure planner,
public consultation requirements,
the information that must be included in a summary required to be published by the infrastructure planner under subsection (1A).

heading.b: Consumer trustee may authorise REZ network infrastructure projects or amend authorisations

block.txt: If the infrastructure planner recommends, under section 30(1)(b), a REZ network infrastructure project for authorisation, the consumer trustee must decide to—
authorise the project in accordance with the recommendation, or
refuse to authorise the project.
If the infrastructure planner recommends, under section 30(2B)(a), an amendment to the terms of an authorisation, the consumer trustee must decide to—
authorise the amendment in accordance with the recommendation, or
refuse to authorise the amendment.
The consumer trustee—

must consider the development pathway contained in the most recently published infrastructure investment objectives report (the current development pathway) when deciding whether to authorise a REZ network infrastructure project under subsection (1), and
may consider the current development pathway when deciding whether to authorise an amendment under subsection (2).
The regulations may make further provision about the following—
the exercise of the consumer trustee’s functions under this section,
requiring the infrastructure planner to give information to the consumer trustee.

heading.b: Maximum capital costs amount for authorised REZ network infrastructure projects

block.txt: For each authorised REZ network infrastructure project, the consumer trustee must, by written notice to the regulator, set a maximum amount for the prudent, efficient and reasonable capital costs for development and construction of the project.
If the infrastructure planner asks, under section 30(2B)(b), the consumer trustee to amend the maximum capital costs amount, the consumer trustee must decide to—
amend, by written notice to the regulator, the maximum capital costs amount, or
refuse to amend the maximum capital costs amount.

In deciding whether to amend the maximum capital costs amount under subsection (2), the consumer trustee must have regard to any relevant amendments authorised by the consumer trustee under section 30AA(2)(a).
The consumer trustee must—
give the Minister written notice of the maximum capital costs amount as soon as practicable after giving written notice of the amount to the regulator under subsection (1), and
give the Minister written notice of an amended maximum capital costs amount as soon as practicable after giving written notice of the amended amount to the regulator under subsection (2).
The consumer trustee must not disclose the maximum capital costs amount to any person other than—
the regulator under subsection (1) or (2), or
the Minister under subsection (4).
The regulator must not disclose the maximum capital costs amount to any person.
The Minister may, by written notice (a Ministerial disclosure notice), disclose the maximum capital costs amount to a person (a recipient) at any time.

The Minister may disclose the maximum capital costs amount under subsection (7) subject to conditions relating to the further disclosure and confidentiality of the maximum capital costs amount, including conditions—
authorising a recipient to disclose the maximum capital costs amount to a specified person or class of persons, or
providing for the way in which, and conditions on which, a recipient may disclose the maximum capital costs amount, or
requiring persons to whom a recipient discloses the maximum capital costs amount to keep the maximum capital costs amount confidential.
A recipient must not disclose the maximum capital costs amount to a person unless the disclosure—
is authorised by the Ministerial disclosure notice, and
otherwise complies with the conditions of the Ministerial disclosure notice.
A person to whom a recipient discloses the maximum capital costs amount—
must not disclose the maximum capital costs amount to a person, and
must comply with the conditions of the Ministerial disclosure notice.
The regulations may make further provision about the following—
the exercise of the consumer trustee’s functions under this section,
requiring the infrastructure planner to give information to the consumer trustee.

heading.b: Appointment of network operators to carry out REZ network infrastructure projects
Infrastructure planner may appoint network operators to carry out REZ network infrastructure projects

block.txt: The infrastructure planner may appoint a network operator to carry out a REZ network infrastructure project.
The infrastructure planner may, at any time, make one or more appointments for one or more network operators under subsection (1) in relation to the REZ network infrastructure project.
The regulations may make further provision about the exercise of the infrastructure planner’s functions under this section, including about—
eligibility criteria for network operators who may be appointed, and
the selection and appointment of network operators.

heading.b: Infrastructure planner may recommend Minister direct authorised REZ network infrastructure projects be carried out

block.txt: The infrastructure planner may recommend to the Minister that the Minister direct a network operator to carry out an authorised REZ network infrastructure project.

The infrastructure planner may, at any time, recommend one or more directions be given to one or more network operators under subsection (1) in relation to the authorised REZ network infrastructure project.

The regulations may make further provision about the exercise of the infrastructure planner’s functions under this section, including the circumstances in which the infrastructure planner must not make a recommendation to the Minister under subsection (1).

heading.b: Directions to carry out network infrastructure projects
Minister may direct network infrastructure projects be carried out

block.txt: The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, direct a network operator to carry out—
a REZ network infrastructure project, or
a priority network infrastructure project.
A direction must specify the following—
the network operator to whom the direction applies,
the location and description of the infrastructure project,
the date by which the network operator, taking all reasonable steps, must comply with the direction,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
A direction may specify the following—
the requirements for the development or construction of the infrastructure project,
the staging or sequencing of the planning, design, financing, construction or commissioning of the infrastructure project,
the requirements for the operation or maintenance of infrastructure relating to the infrastructure project,
whether another direction may be made about the infrastructure project in accordance with section 35C,

that the network operator must facilitate or permit another network operator carrying out work on infrastructure owned or leased by the network operator in accordance with a direction to the other network operator under subsection (4B),
other matters the Minister considers relevant.
The Minister must consult with a network operator before giving the network operator a direction.
The Minister must give a direction only if satisfied that—
it is in the public interest, and
it is consistent with the objects of this Act.
One or more directions to one or more network operators may be given at any time under this section in relation to an infrastructure project.
A direction under this section may direct a network operator to commission, operate or maintain infrastructure not owned or leased by the network operator.

A direction under subsection (4B) does not have effect until a direction under subsection (2A)(e) directs the other network operator that owns or leases the infrastructure to facilitate or permit the network operator to commission, operate or maintain the infrastructure.
The regulations may make further provision about the following—
the exercise of the Minister’s functions under this section,
the classes of renewable energy zones in relation to which a direction may be given,
the classes of authorised REZ network infrastructure projects and priority network infrastructure projects in relation to which a direction may be given.

heading.b: Directions for authorised REZ network infrastructure projects

block.txt: The Minister may give a network operator a direction under section 32(1)(a) only if the infrastructure planner has recommended the giving of the direction under section 31B.
Before giving the network operator the direction, the Minister must consult with the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces.
The regulations may make further provision about the following—
the exercise of the Minister’s functions under this section,
the eligibility criteria and selection process for network operators who may be directed to carry out authorised REZ network infrastructure projects,
the matters the Minister may or must consider when deciding whether to direct a network operator to carry out an authorised REZ network infrastructure project.

heading.b: Directions for priority network infrastructure projects

block.txt: Before directing a network operator to carry out a priority network infrastructure project, the Minister must consult with the following—
the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces,
AEMO,
the regulator,
distribution network service providers and transmission network service providers.
The Minister must not direct a network operator to carry out a priority network infrastructure project unless the Minister has considered the following—
existing network infrastructure in the area in which the priority network infrastructure project will be located,
land use planning, environmental and heritage matters,
the views of the local community in the area in which the priority network infrastructure project will be located,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
The Minister must not direct a network operator to carry out a priority network infrastructure project unless the Minister is satisfied that—
it is an appropriate response to—
a target breach identified in an energy security target monitor report, or
a forecast shortfall in reliability or system security services identified in a report prepared under or published in accordance with the National Electricity Rules, Chapter 5, 6 or 6A, and
it is in the public interest, and
any conditions prescribed by the regulations are complied with.
The obligation of a network operator to comply with a direction under section 32 does not commence until the first of the following occurs—

the Minister gives written notice to the network operator that the Minister is satisfied that reasonable interim financial arrangements are in place for the network operator to commence carrying out the direction before a determination is made under section 38,
the regulator makes a determination under section 38 in relation to the direction.
Before giving a written notice under subsection (1)(a), the Minister must—
consult with the network operator, and
have regard to the interests of the network operator and NSW electricity customers.

Section 34(1) and (2) does not apply to the amendment of a direction under section 32 if the amendment does not include a material change to the location or description of the infrastructure project as specified in the direction.

A direction under section 32 in relation to a priority network infrastructure project must not be amended in a way that would materially change the location or description of the infrastructure project as specified in the direction.
Subsection (2) does not affect the power to revoke the direction or make another direction under section 32 in relation to the infrastructure project.
This section applies to an infrastructure project for which—
a direction has been made, and
there has been no material change to the location or description of the infrastructure project as specified in the initial direction for the project.
Section 34(1) and (2) does not apply to the making of a further direction about an infrastructure project to which this section applies if—
the direction does not make a material change to the location or description of the infrastructure project as specified in the initial direction, and
the initial direction specified that a further direction about the infrastructure project may be made in accordance with this section.
In this section—
direction means a direction made under section 32.
initial direction, in relation to an infrastructure project, means the first direction made in connection with the infrastructure project.
A network operator to whom a direction is given under section 32 must not fail to comply with the direction.
Maximum penalty—
for a corporation—18,000 penalty units, or
for an individual—3,500 penalty units.

If a network operator to whom a direction is given under section 32 holds a licence under the Electricity Supply Act 1995 it is a condition of the licence that the licensee complies with the direction.
A person cannot, in relation to the same act or omission, be both—
prosecuted for an offence against subsection (1), and
dealt with by the Minister or the Tribunal for a contravention of a licence condition under the Electricity Supply Act 1995, Schedule 2, clause 8 or 8A.
A person must not bring proceedings for the prosecution of an offence against subsection (1) in relation to an act or omission unless the person—
has considered whether the act or omission has been or is likely to be the subject of another penalty or action under the National Electricity (NSW) Law, and
is satisfied that it is nevertheless appropriate to bring the proceedings.

heading.b: Directors and managers liable for failures to comply with directions

block.txt: If a corporation contravenes section 35(1), each of the following persons is to be treated as having contravened the section if the person knowingly authorised or permitted the contravention—
a person who is a director of the corporation, or
a person who is concerned in the management of the corporation.

A person may, under this section, be proceeded against and convicted for a contravention of section 35(1) whether or not the corporation has been proceeded against or convicted for a contravention of the section.
Nothing in this section affects any liability imposed on a corporation for an offence against section 35(1) committed by the corporation.
In this division—
adjustment, of amounts, includes an adjustment of amounts under a provision included in a determination, whether under section 38(3) or otherwise.
authorisation means—
an appointment by the infrastructure planner under section 31A(1) in relation to an authorised REZ network infrastructure project, or
an authorisation by the Minister under section 36(2), or
a direction given by the Minister under section 32 to carry out an infrastructure project.
network operator includes persons referred to in section 36(1A), but only for the purpose specified in the subsection.
This Division applies to a network operator who is subject to an authorisation.
This division also applies to the following persons, but only for the purpose of an adjustment of amounts—
a network operator who was subject to an authorisation,
a person who was a network operator subject to an authorisation.
The Minister may authorise a network operator to carry out a priority network infrastructure project for the purposes of this Division.
One or more authorisations for one or more network operators may be made at any time under subsection (2) for a priority network infrastructure project.

Before authorising a network operator under subsection (2), the Minister must consult with the persons and bodies specified in section 34(1) and be satisfied of the matters specified in section 34(3).

heading.b: Regulator to take into account principles

block.txt: In exercising functions under this Division, the regulator is to take into account the following principles—
a network operator is entitled to recover the prudent, efficient and reasonable costs incurred by the network operator for carrying out the infrastructure project,
incentives should be given to network operators to promote economic efficiency,

a network operator is entitled to revenue for the ongoing ownership, control or operation of an infrastructure project that is commensurate with the regulatory and commercial risks to the network operator,
a network operator is entitled to be informed of material issues being considered by the regulator under this Division,
other principles prescribed by the regulations.
The regulations may make further provision for or with respect to the principles in subsection (1).

heading.b: Regulator to determine amount payable to or by network operators for network infrastructure projects

block.txt: The regulator is to determine the amount payable to a network operator to whom this Division applies.
A determination is to include amounts for different components applicable to the relevant authorisation, including—
repayment of capital costs as determined under the transmission efficiency test,
the return on capital costs that have not been repaid,
an allowance for operating costs,
other components prescribed by the regulations.
A determination may include provision for the adjustment of amounts on the basis of differences between the estimated and actual capital costs.
An adjustment provision included in a determination may provide that amounts may be payable by a network operator to the scheme financial vehicle in specified circumstances.
To avoid doubt—
a provision of a determination about the adjustment of amounts may have effect after the expiry of the relevant authorisation, and
if a provision in a determination about the adjustment of amounts requires a determination to be reviewed and remade, the following may occur after the expiry of the relevant authorisation—
a determination may be remade,
a provision in a determination about the adjustment of amounts may have effect and provide for amounts to be payable by a network operator to the scheme financial vehicle.

Before making a determination, the regulator is to calculate the prudent, efficient and reasonable capital costs of the network operator for development and construction of the network infrastructure project, which is referred to as the transmission efficiency test.
The regulator is to publish guidelines on its website about the transmission efficiency test.

If a determination relates to the amount payable to a network operator appointed under section 31A to carry out a REZ network infrastructure project, the amount calculated under subsection (4) must not exceed the difference between the maximum capital costs amount for the project and the sum of the following—
any amounts paid or payable, under another determination for the project, to a network operator for the capital costs of development and construction of the project,
any amounts that have been paid, or are likely to be paid, out of the Fund to the infrastructure planner for the project.
To avoid doubt, it is declared that subsection (6) does not apply to the amount determined by the regulator under subsection (4) as adjusted from time to time in accordance with—
the adjustment of amounts provided for in the determination under subsection (3), or
the regulations made under subsection (10).

The regulator may, by written notice to a network operator, require the network operator to provide information to the regulator that the regulator considers necessary to enable the regulator to make a determination.
A notice under subsection (7) must specify the following—
the information required to be provided,
the form in which the information is to be provided,
the time within which the information is to be provided.
A network operator must not, without lawful excuse, fail to comply with a requirement made of the network operator under subsection (7).
Maximum penalty—2,000 penalty units for a corporation or 100 penalty units for an individual
If a network operator to whom a notice under subsection (7) applies holds a licence under the Electricity Supply Act 1995, it is a condition of the licence that the licensee complies with the notice.

A person cannot be both prosecuted for an offence against subsection (9) and dealt with by the Minister for a contravention of a licence condition under the Electricity Supply Act 1995, Schedule 2, clause 8 in relation to the same act or omission.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the following—
the making of a determination by the regulator,

the matters the regulator is to take into account in making a determination, including any loans or other financial arrangements entered into by the network operator for the purposes of carrying out the infrastructure project,
the information required to be provided to the regulator by a network operator,
the information to be included in a determination,
other matters relating to the transmission efficiency test,
other matters relating to a determination by the regulator.
The scheme financial vehicle is required to pay the network operator the amount the network operator is entitled to in accordance with the regulator’s determination.
A network operator must pay the scheme financial vehicle the amount the scheme financial vehicle is entitled to in accordance with the regulator’s determination.

The regulations may make provision for or with respect to circumstances in which the scheme financial vehicle is not required to pay the network operator if the network operator is entitled to receive an equivalent amount under the National Electricity (NSW) Law.
The regulator is, in accordance with the regulations, to remake a determination under section 38—
once every 5 years, and
at any time the consumer trustee directs.
The regulator may review and remake a determination at any time, subject to the regulations.
Section 38(6) does not apply in relation to the review or remaking of the determination.

heading.b: Application of National Electricity (NSW) Law and National Electricity Rules

block.txt: The regulations may modify the application of, or disapply, a provision of the National Electricity (NSW) Law or the National Electricity Rules to the extent reasonably necessary to achieve the objects of this Act and—
to enable a network operator to whom this Division applies to carry out an infrastructure project, or
to enable a network operator to whom this Division applies to—
receive payment from the scheme financial vehicle to which the operator is entitled under this Division, or
recover costs for carrying out an infrastructure project under the National Electricity Rules, or
to enable a network operator to transition between the arrangements specified in paragraph (b)(i) and (ii), or
to ensure a network operator does not receive payment under both arrangements specified in paragraph (b)(i) and (ii).

A regulation under this section that affects the operation or safety of network infrastructure may not be made unless the Minister has consulted with distribution network service providers and transmission network service providers.
A regulation under this section that affects AEMO in the exercise of its function may not be made without the concurrence of AEMO.

The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the effect of the transfer of network infrastructure by a network operator to whom this Division applies (the transferor) to another person (the transferee).
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision for or with respect to the circumstances in which the transferee is taken to be a network operator to whom this Division applies.

heading.b: Application of National Electricity (NSW) Law and National Electricity Rules in relation to system security services

block.txt: The regulations may modify the application of, or disapply, a provision of the National Electricity (NSW) Law or the National Electricity Rules to the extent reasonably necessary to achieve the objects of this Act and to enable the planning, provision and management of system security services in connection with network infrastructure, including infrastructure not owned by the system strength service provider.

A regulation under this section that affects the operation or safety of network infrastructure may not be made unless the Minister has consulted with distribution network service providers and transmission network service providers.
A regulation under this section that affects AEMO in the exercise of its functions may not be made without the concurrence of AEMO.
This Part applies to the following infrastructure—
generation infrastructure that involves generation from a renewable energy source and that has a generation capacity of not less than 30 megawatts,
long-duration storage infrastructure for storage of electricity that—
consists of storage units with a relevant capacity that can be dispatched for at least 8 hours, and
is scheduled by AEMO in the central dispatch process under the National Electricity Rules,
firming infrastructure that is scheduled by AEMO in the central dispatch process under the National Electricity Rules.
This Part does not apply to infrastructure that is part of a committed infrastructure project.
In this Part—

committed infrastructure project means a project that was identified as committed or existing in a generation information page published by AEMO under the National Electricity Rules on or before 14 November 2019.
maximum capacity, for infrastructure, means the amount, in megawatts, shown as the maximum capacity for generation for the infrastructure in the NEM registration and exemption list.
NEM registration and exemption list means the document titled NEM registration and exemption list published by AEMO or a document that replaces the document.
registered capacity has the same meaning as in Chapter 4A of the National Electricity Rules.
relevant capacity, for long-duration storage infrastructure for storage of electricity, means the lower of the following—
the registered capacity for the infrastructure,
the maximum capacity for the infrastructure.
reliability standard means the reliability standard implemented by AEMO under the National Electricity Rules that is prescribed by the regulations.
renewable energy source means an energy source specified in section 17(1)(a)–(s) of the Renewable Energy (Electricity) Act 2000 of the Commonwealth as in force on the commencement of this section.
The infrastructure investment objectives are—
the overall objectives for the construction of infrastructure to which this Part applies, and

the minimum objectives for the period ending on 31 December 2029 (the 2030 objective investment period) for the construction of generation infrastructure and long-duration storage infrastructure to which this Part applies, and
the minimum objective for the period ending on 31 December 2033 (the 2034 objective investment period) for the construction of long-duration storage infrastructure to which this part applies.
The overall objectives are—
construction of generation infrastructure that is necessary to minimise electricity costs for NSW electricity customers, and
construction of long-duration storage infrastructure that is necessary to meet the reliability standard, and
construction of firming infrastructure that is necessary to meet the energy security target and the reliability standard.
The minimum objectives for the 2030 objective investment period are—
construction of generation infrastructure that generates at least the same amount of electricity in a year as—
8 gigawatts of generation capacity from the New England renewable energy zone, and
3 gigawatts of generation capacity from the Central-West Orana renewable energy zone, and
1 additional gigawatt of generation capacity, and
construction of long-duration storage infrastructure with at least—
storage of 16 gigawatt hours, and
capacity of 2 gigawatts.

The minimum objective for the 2034 objective investment period is the construction of long-duration storage infrastructure, including long-duration storage infrastructure constructed during the 2030 objective investment period, with a total storage of at least 28 gigawatt hours.
Committed infrastructure projects are not to be counted towards the infrastructure investment objectives.
The consumer trustee is to prepare a report about the infrastructure investment objectives that contains—
the development pathway for the infrastructure to which this Part applies that is required to be constructed over the following 20 years to achieve the infrastructure investment objectives, and

a plan for the competitive tenders that the consumer trustee will conduct during the following 10 years to give effect to the development pathway, including when tenders will be conducted and the classes of LTES agreements for which a tender will be conducted, and
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
The consumer trustee is to prepare a report—
as soon as practicable after the commencement of this section, and
approximately every 2 years after the first report.

The consumer trustee is also to prepare a report as soon as practicable after being directed by the Minister under section 47(2) to conduct a competitive tender for LTES agreements for firming infrastructure.
The regulations may prescribe the matters that the consumer trustee is to take into account in preparing the report.
The report is to be published on the consumer trustee’s website.
The consumer trustee is to exercise its functions under this Part on the basis of the reports prepared under this section.

heading.b: Meaning of “long-term energy service agreement” or “LTES agreement”

block.txt: A long-term energy service agreement or LTES agreement is an agreement entered into between the scheme financial vehicle and a person (the LTES operator) under which—
the LTES operator constructs and operates infrastructure to which this Part applies as specified in the agreement, and
if the LTES operator does this, the LTES operator may periodically opt to exercise a derivative arrangement.
An LTES agreement must—
provide for the construction and operation of the infrastructure to which the agreement relates if the LTES operator wishes to exercise an option under the agreement, and
divide the term of the agreement into periods of no less than 1 financial year, and
give the LTES operator an option to exercise a derivative arrangement, and
require notice to be given to the scheme financial vehicle of a proposal to exercise an option that is not less than the minimum notice period prescribed by the regulations, and
provide for the repayment to the scheme financial vehicle of amounts paid because of the exercise of an option in certain circumstances set out in the agreement, and
contain or deal with other matters prescribed by the regulations.
The consumer trustee must conduct a competitive tender for LTES agreements unless the regulator otherwise authorises generally or in a particular case.
The consumer trustee must not conduct a competitive tender for LTES agreements for firming infrastructure unless directed by the Minister.
A competitive tender must be carried out in accordance with—
any requirements prescribed by the regulations, and
the rules made by the consumer trustee under this section.

A tender bid must, unless exempted by the regulations, include information about how the proposal will create employment and support industry in New South Wales if the person enters into an LTES agreement.
Before conducting a competitive tender, the consumer trustee must make rules that are consistent with the regulations to deal with the following matters—
the eligibility criteria for making a tender bid,
the notification of the opening of the competitive tender,
the procedure for making a tender bid, including the information required to be included in a bid,
the fee payable for making a bid and requirements for bonds or other security,
the assessment of a tender bid by the consumer trustee,
other matters the consumer trustee considers necessary,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
Before making rules, the consumer trustee is to consult with the regulator.
The rules are to be published in the Gazette.
The consumer trustee must make recommendations to the scheme financial vehicle about the LTES agreements that the scheme financial vehicle may enter into.
In making a recommendation, the financial value of LTES agreements is to be the primary consideration for the consumer trustee.

The consumer trustee must not recommend the making of an LTES agreement that relates to generation infrastructure specified in section 43(1)(a) that is not, or will not be, part of a renewable energy zone, unless the consumer trustee is satisfied that the LTES agreement shows outstanding merit.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to—
the circumstances in which an LTES agreement shows outstanding merit for the purposes of subsection (3), and
the matters to be taken into account by the consumer trustee in making recommendations.

heading.b: Operation of long-term energy service agreements

block.txt: An LTES agreement may not be made, unless the consumer trustee recommends the making of the LTES agreement.
The regulations may prescribe further circumstances in which an LTES agreement may not be made.
An LTES agreement remains in force for the term of the agreement unless the agreement is sooner suspended or terminated.

heading.b: Terms and conditions of LTES agreements

block.txt: The consumer trustee is to determine the terms and conditions of an LTES agreement, subject to any requirements prescribed by the regulations.
An LTES operator is required to provide information to the Minister every year about the extent to which the LTES operator is creating employment and supporting industry in New South Wales.
The information is to be provided in a form prescribed by the regulations.
The Minister is to prepare a yearly report summarising the information received from LTES operators and is to table the report in each House of Parliament.
In determining the terms and conditions of an LTES agreement, the consumer trustee is to take into account the following principles—
to align the financial incentives offered under LTES agreements with the changing needs of the electricity system,
to adopt, to the maximum extent possible, the conventions and standards in relation to similar agreements in the national electricity market,
to ensure that LTES agreements allow for future changes in the national electricity market,
to ensure that LTES agreements are consistent with the risk management framework under Division 5,
other principles prescribed by the regulations.

The regulations may make further provision for or with respect to the terms and conditions of an LTES agreement, including in relation to a requirement for a bond or other security to be provided by the LTES operator under the LTES agreement.
This section does not prevent the parties to an LTES agreement from agreeing to additional terms and conditions.
In this section—
national electricity market has the same meaning as in the National Electricity (NSW) Law.
The consumer trustee is to prepare a risk management framework to protect the financial interests of NSW electricity customers in connection with the risks associated with LTES agreements.
The risk management framework may provide for the functions of the consumer trustee, the financial trustee, the scheme financial vehicle and the regulator under the framework.
The risk management framework must be approved by the regulator.
The approved risk management framework is to be published on the consumer trustee’s website.
Despite subsection (4), the consumer trustee is not required to publish a part of the risk management framework if—
the consumer trustee considers it is in the public interest not to publish the part, and
the consumer trustee has the approval of the regulator to not publish the part.
The Minister may—
require the regulator to review an approved risk management framework, and
require the consumer trustee to amend the risk management framework in accordance with a recommendation by the regulator arising from the review.
The regulations may prescribe requirements for the risk management framework.
The scheme financial vehicle may enter into a risk management contract for the purposes of this Part if it is consistent with the risk management framework that is in force under this Division.
A risk management contract may be a derivative arrangement.
Subject to the regulations, the term of the contract and the circumstances in which it can be renewed, extended, suspended or terminated are to be included in the contract.
The scheme financial vehicle is to establish and maintain an electricity infrastructure fund for the purposes of this Act (the Fund).
Money held in the Fund is to be paid into an account kept with an authorised deposit-taking institution.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the administration of the Fund.
The following are payable into the Fund, subject to any requirements prescribed by the regulations—
all money received by the scheme financial vehicle from a distribution network service provider under a contribution order,
all money advanced by the scheme financial vehicle for the Fund,
all money paid to the scheme financial vehicle under an LTES agreement or a risk management contract,
all money paid to the scheme financial vehicle as fees by participants in an access scheme,
all money paid to the scheme financial vehicle by a network operator under a determination under Part 5, Division 3,
the proceeds of investment of money in the Fund,
all money received from voluntary contributions to the Fund made by a person or body,
other money required to be paid into the Fund by or under this or another Act or law.
The following are payable from the Fund, subject to any requirements prescribed by the regulations—

money required to meet the liabilities of the scheme financial vehicle under this Act, including, but not limited to, liabilities for payments by the scheme financial vehicle under an access scheme, section 39, an LTES competitive tender, an LTES agreement or a risk management contract,
money authorised by the Minister to cover the administrative costs of the scheme financial vehicle,

money as payment to the consumer trustee, financial trustee, infrastructure planner and regulator, as required in the instrument of appointment or otherwise authorised by the Minister, to enable the exercise of their functions under this Act,
money directed or authorised to be paid from the Fund by or under this or another Act or law.

heading.b: Regulator to make annual contribution determinations

block.txt: The regulator is to determine an amount for a financial year (a contribution determination) that is required for the scheme financial vehicle to be able to make the payments from the Fund that are required under this Act, including the amount required for the scheme financial vehicle to meet its liabilities as they fall due.
The purpose of the contribution determination is to determine the amount required to be recovered from distribution network service providers.
The amount determined by the regulator is to include—
a minimum prudent cash balance for the Fund, and
the amount required to be paid by each distribution network service provider.
A contribution determination must contain—
details of how the contribution determination was made, and
other information prescribed by the regulations.

A contribution determination must be published in the Gazette no later than 28 February before the beginning of the financial year to which the contribution determination is to apply, unless the Minister approves a later date.
In making a contribution determination, the regulator must—
consult with the financial trustee, and
take into account the matters prescribed by the regulations.

The scheme financial vehicle must, if requested by the regulator, provide the regulator with the information the regulator considers necessary to enable the regulator to make a contribution determination.
The regulator may, by further order published in the Gazette, vary a contribution determination if it appears to the regulator that—
the scheme financial vehicle will not be able to meet its liabilities as they fall due, or
the cash balance of the Fund has fallen, or is likely to fall, below the minimum prudent cash balance specified in the determination.
The regulator is to publish guidelines on its website about the exercise of the regulator’s functions under this section.
An order varying a contribution determination may be made before or during the financial year to which the determination applies or during the following financial year, but not later.

heading.b: Contributions by distribution network service providers
