block.txt: The scheme financial vehicle may, by order served on a distribution network service provider (a contribution order), require the distribution network service provider to pay a specified amount into the Fund.

The amount specified in a contribution order is to be the amount specified in the regulator’s contribution determination for the distribution network service provider, subject to any requirements prescribed by the regulations.

The scheme financial vehicle may determine the amount specified in a contribution order on its own initiative if the regulator does not publish a contribution determination for the financial year within the period required under section 56(5).

The amount determined by the scheme financial vehicle under subsection (3) is not to exceed the amount reasonably required to enable the scheme financial vehicle to meets its liabilities as they fall due.

An amount payable by a distribution network service provider under a contribution order is recoverable by the scheme financial vehicle as a debt in any court of competent jurisdiction for payment into the Fund.

The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the circumstances in which a distribution network service provider is or is not authorised to recover part of the amount payable under a contribution order from a person who is exempt from the energy savings scheme under clause 22 of Schedule 4A to the Electricity Supply Act 1995 or from a person who buys electricity to use in the production of hydrogen energy.
The Minister may appoint a person or body as the energy security target monitor.
In the absence of an appointment, the Secretary must exercise the functions of the energy security target monitor.
The energy security target monitor has the following functions—
the functions prescribed by the regulations,
other functions conferred or imposed on the monitor by or under this or another Act or law.
In the exercise of functions under this Act, the energy security target monitor is not subject to the direction or control of the Minister.
The Minister is to appoint a person or body as the consumer trustee.
In the absence of an appointment, the Secretary must exercise the functions of the consumer trustee.
The consumer trustee is to act independently and in the long-term financial interests of NSW electricity customers.
The consumer trustee has the following functions—
to advise the Minister and the infrastructure planner in relation to proposed and declared renewable energy zones and proposed and required REZ network infrastructure projects,
to negotiate, in accordance with any requirements prescribed by the regulations, with a person in relation to LTES agreements,
other functions prescribed by the regulations,
other functions conferred or imposed on the consumer trustee by or under this or another Act or law.
In the exercise of functions under this Act, the consumer trustee is not subject to the control or direction of the Minister.
The consumer trustee is to appoint a person or body as the financial trustee.
The financial trustee has the following functions—
to administer the scheme financial vehicle,
to advise the regulator in relation to contribution determinations,
other functions prescribed by the regulations,
other functions conferred or imposed on the financial trustee by or under this or another Act or law.
In the exercise of functions under this Act, the financial trustee is not subject to the control or direction of the consumer trustee or the Minister.

Within 3 months of the commencement of this section, the financial trustee is to establish the scheme financial vehicle as a company limited by shares under the Corporations Act 2001 of the Commonwealth.
Despite subsection (1), the regulations may authorise the financial trustee to instead be the scheme financial vehicle.
The financial trustee is to arrange for all the shares in a company referred to in subsection (1) to be held on trust by the financial trustee for the purposes of this Act.
The scheme financial vehicle is to act in a commercially reasonable and prudent way under any contract or agreement made under this Act.

If the appointment of a person or body as financial trustee under section 61 is terminated or the person or body resigns the appointment, the person or body is to arrange for its shares in the scheme financial vehicle to be transferred to the new financial trustee.

The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the transfer of shares following the termination or resignation of the appointment of the financial trustee in circumstances where the financial trustee is the scheme financial vehicle.

A court assessing liquidated damages in relation to a breach of a contract to which the scheme financial vehicle is a party is to take into account damages suffered by NSW electricity customers as if they were damages suffered by the scheme financial vehicle.
The Minister is to appoint a person as the infrastructure planner.
Different infrastructure planners may be appointed to exercise different functions or functions in relation to different renewable energy zones or different parts of renewable energy zones.
An infrastructure planner may be appointed to exercise functions in relation to an access area or part of an access area.
An infrastructure planner may be appointed to exercise functions in relation to a priority network infrastructure project.

The functions of an infrastructure planner in relation to a renewable energy zone or part of a renewable energy zone are to be exercised by the Energy Corporation at any time during which a person is not appointed as the infrastructure planner for the renewable energy zone or part of the renewable energy zone.

The functions of an infrastructure planner in relation to an access area or part of an access area must be exercised by the Energy Corporation at any time during which a person is not appointed as the infrastructure planner for the access area or part of the access area.
Subject to limitations in the instrument of appointment, an infrastructure planner has the following functions—
to make and enter into contracts or other agreements in connection with the exercise of its functions under this Act,
to investigate, plan, co-ordinate and carry out planning and design of generation infrastructure,
to investigate, plan, co-ordinate and carry out planning, design, construction and operation of storage and network infrastructure,
other functions prescribed by the regulations,
other functions conferred or imposed on the infrastructure planner by or under this or another Act or law.

An infrastructure planner also has the function of identifying, assessing and, if appropriate, recommending to the Minister a network infrastructure project the infrastructure planner considers to be an appropriate response to—
a target breach identified in an energy security target monitor report, or
a forecast shortfall in reliability or system security services identified in a report prepared under or published in accordance with the National Electricity Rules, Chapter 5, 6, or 6A.

If the Energy Corporation is appointed as an infrastructure planner, the Energy Corporation has the functions, as modified by the regulations, that the Corporation has under the Energy and Utilities Administration Act 1987 and may exercise those functions as the infrastructure planner under this Act, to the extent reasonably necessary to—
enable the infrastructure planner to exercise its functions under this Act, and
achieve the objects of this Act.
Sections 11(3) and 12(4) of the Energy and Utilities Administration Act 1987 do not apply to the Energy Corporation when exercising functions under subsection (5).
If the Energy Corporation is appointed as an infrastructure planner, it may—
form, or participate in the formation of, a private subsidiary corporation, and
acquire interests in private subsidiary corporations, and
sell or otherwise dispose of interests in private subsidiary corporations.
In the exercise of functions under this Act, an infrastructure planner is subject to the control or direction of the Minister.
In this section—
private subsidiary corporation means a corporation within the meaning of the Corporations Act 2001 of the Commonwealth in which the Energy Corporation has a controlling interest.
The Minister is to appoint one of the following as the regulator—
the AER,
the Tribunal,
a person prescribed by the regulations.
More than 1 regulator may be appointed.
The functions of the regulator are to be exercised by the Tribunal at any time during which a person or body is not appointed as the regulator.
Subject to limitations in the instrument of appointment, a regulator has the following functions—
to issue guidelines in relation to the exercise of functions by the persons and bodies appointed under this Act,
other functions prescribed by the regulations,
other functions conferred or imposed on the regulator by or under this or another Act or law.
In the exercise of functions under this Act, a regulator is not subject to the control or direction of the Minister.
In this Division—
appointor means—
in relation to the appointment of the financial trustee—the consumer trustee, and
in relation to the appointment of another person or body—the Minister.
A person or body may be appointed under this Part only if the appointor is satisfied that the person or body—
is fit and proper, and
has the necessary qualifications and experience.
Subsection (1) does not apply to the appointment of the following—
the AER,
AEMO,
the Tribunal,
the Energy Corporation.
A person or body is appointed under this Part—
for the term specified in the instrument of appointment, if any, and
subject to the terms and conditions specified in the instrument of appointment and prescribed by the regulations.

A person or body appointed under this Part is entitled to be paid by the scheme financial vehicle the amount determined from time to time by the appointor in accordance with the regulations for the exercise of functions under this Act.
The regulations may make further provision for or with respect to the following—
the appointment of persons or bodies under this Part,
the circumstances in which a person or body is not considered fit and proper,
the necessary qualifications and experience for appointment,
limitations on the functions of a person or body appointed under this Part,
the amounts determined as payment for the exercise of functions by a person or body appointed under this Part.
The regulator is to audit the performance of the following—
the consumer trustee,
the financial trustee,
the scheme financial vehicle,
the infrastructure planner.
The Minister may require the regulator to conduct an audit under this section.
The Minister may appoint a person to audit the performance of the energy security target monitor or the regulator.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to an audit under this section, including the following—
the matters that may be the subject of an audit,
for an audit of the performance of the energy security target monitor and the regulator —the persons who may be appointed to conduct the audit,
the functions that may be exercised by the person conducting an audit,
the conduct of an audit,
reporting on an audit, including the publication of an audit report.
The appointor may suspend or terminate the appointment of a person or body under this Part by giving written notice to the person or body.

The appointor may suspend or terminate the appointment of a person or body only if an audit of the performance of the person or body carried out under section 67 finds incompetence, misconduct or incapacity.
Before terminating the appointment of a person or body under this Part, the appointor must—
advise the person or body in writing that the person or body’s performance is unsatisfactory and the basis on which it is unsatisfactory, and
provide the person or body with an opportunity to make submissions and consider the submissions received.
The Governor may terminate the appointment of a person or body under this Part on the address of both Houses of Parliament.
To avoid doubt, a person or body appointed under this Part cannot be removed from office under Part 6 of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013.
A person or body appointed under this Part may resign the appointment by providing 6 months written notice to the appointor or as agreed to by the appointor.

The consumer trustee, the financial trustee and the infrastructure planner must, as soon as reasonably practicable after the end of each financial year, each provide the regulator with a report on the exercise of the person or body’s functions under this Act during the financial year.
The regulator must prepare an annual report on the exercise of functions under this Act by the consumer trustee, the financial trustee, the infrastructure planner and the regulator itself.
The annual report must contain the information required by the Minister.
The regulator must provide the annual report to the Minister no later than 4 months after the end of the financial year to which the report relates.
The regulator must publish the annual report on its website as soon as reasonably practicable after providing it to the Minister.

The infrastructure planner may delegate its functions, other than this power of delegation, to any person.
The consumer trustee, the financial trustee and the regulator may delegate any of their functions, other than this power of delegation, to a person of a class prescribed by the regulations.

The Secretary may, when exercising a function of the energy security target monitor under section 59(2) or the consumer trustee under section 60(2), delegate the function to an employee of the Department.

The Secretary may subdelegate a function delegated to the Secretary by the Minister under subsection (1) to an authorised person, unless the Minister otherwise provides in the instrument of delegation to the Secretary.
The Secretary may delegate the Secretary’s functions under this Act, other than this power of delegation, to an authorised person.

authorised person means—
an employee of the Department, or
a person, or a person of a class, prescribed by the regulations.
Relevant conduct is conduct that is specifically authorised by this Act for the purposes of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 of the Commonwealth and the Competition Code of New South Wales.

Conduct authorised by this section is authorised only to the extent, if any, that it would otherwise contravene Part IV of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 of the Commonwealth and the Competition Code of New South Wales.

complying with an obligation arising in connection with the requirement, and
exercising or enforcing a right or power arising in connection with the requirement.

making an order under section 29,
giving effect to a requirement under an order under section 29,
conducting a competitive tender for LTES agreements,
offering to enter into and entering into an LTES agreement or risk management contract,
giving effect to a requirement under an LTES agreement or risk management contract,
exercising a function in relation to, or giving effect to a requirement in relation to, the grant, increase or administration of access rights in an access scheme by a person or body other than—
a person or body who holds access rights in the access scheme, or
a person or body applying or competing to hold access rights in the access scheme,
other conduct prescribed by the regulations.

in good faith, and
for the purpose of exercising functions under this Act.
The liability instead attaches to the Crown.

done includes omitted to be done.
liability means civil liability and includes action, claim or demand.
protected person means the following—
the energy security target monitor,
the consumer trustee,
the financial trustee, except in its capacity as the scheme financial vehicle if the financial trustee is prescribed as the scheme financial vehicle by the regulations under section 62(2),
the regulator,
the infrastructure planner, except in relation to the following—
the administration of an access scheme in a renewable energy zone or access area,
the carrying out of construction or development of storage and network infrastructure,
the Secretary when exercising the functions of—
the energy security target monitor under section 59(2), or
the consumer trustee under section 60(2),
a person acting under the direction of a person or body specified in paragraphs (a)–(e1), other than the scheme financial vehicle.

A person must not, for the purposes of this Act, give to any of the following persons or bodies, whether orally or in writing, information or a document that the person knows to be false or misleading in a material particular, unless the person informs the person or body of that fact—
the consumer trustee,
the financial trustee,
the scheme financial vehicle,
the regulator,
the infrastructure planner.
Maximum penalty—2,000 penalty units for a corporation or 100 penalty units for an individual.

with the consent of the person from whom the information was obtained, or
in connection with the administration or execution of this Act, or
for the purposes of legal proceedings arising out of this Act, or
in accordance with a requirement of the Ombudsman Act 1974, or
with other lawful excuse.
Maximum penalty—2,000 penalty units for a corporation or 100 penalty units for an individual.
This section does not apply to information that is protected information under section 18.
An authorised officer may issue a penalty notice to a person if it appears to the officer that the person has committed a penalty notice offence.
A penalty notice offence is an offence against this Act or the regulations that is prescribed by the regulations as a penalty notice offence.
The Fines Act 1996 applies to a penalty notice issued under this section.

The Fines Act 1996 provides that, if a person issued with a penalty notice does not wish to have the matter determined by a court, the person may pay the amount specified in the notice and is not liable to any further proceedings for the alleged offence.

The amount payable under a penalty notice issued under this section is the amount prescribed for the alleged offence by the regulations, not exceeding the maximum amount of penalty that could be imposed for the offence by a court.
This section does not limit the operation of any other provision of, or made under, this or any other Act relating to proceedings that may be taken in respect of offences.
In this section—
authorised officer means the following—
the energy security target monitor,
a person of a class prescribed by the regulations.
Proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations are to be dealt with summarily before the Local Court.
Proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations may instead be dealt with summarily before the Supreme Court in its summary jurisdiction.
Proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations may be instituted at any time within 2 years after the commission of the offence.

The maximum penalty that may be imposed by the Local Court in proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations is 100 penalty units for a corporation and 50 penalty units for an individual.

The maximum penalty that may be imposed by the Supreme Court in proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations is the maximum penalty specified by the relevant section of this Act, or relevant clause of the regulations, for the offence.
Without limiting section 14 of the Criminal Procedure Act 1986, proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations may be commenced by the regulator.
The Minister is to review this Act to determine whether the policy objectives of the Act remain valid and whether the terms of the Act remain appropriate for securing the objectives.
The review is to be undertaken as soon as possible after the period of 5 years from the commencement of this section.
A report on the outcome of the review is to be tabled in each House of Parliament within 12 months after the end of the period of 5 years.

A regulation may create an offence punishable by a penalty not exceeding 2,000 penalty units for a corporation or 500 penalty units for an individual.

a provision of this Act, or
a provision amending this Act.
A savings or transitional provision consequent on the commencement of a provision must not be made more than 2 years after that commencement.
A savings or transitional provision made consequent on the commencement of a provision is repealed 2 years after that commencement.
A savings or transitional provision made consequent on the commencement of a provision may take effect before that commencement but not before—
for a provision of this Act, the date of assent to this Act, or
for a provision amending this Act, the date of assent to the amending Act.

impose liabilities on a person for anything done or omitted to be done before that publication.
